messages:
Anya Patel: FYI — nightly long-context eval (longctx suite) spiked on the quantized build. Model: xq2-q8, runtime v0.9.3. Failures ~14/50, majority look like truncation/lost instructions in the prefix. Investigating now.

Eval-bot: nightly-run: model=xq2-q8-quantized runtime=0.9.3 total=50 failed=14 longctx_failure_rate=28% top_modes=[truncation:11, misordered_tokens:3] logs: https://internal/evals/1772504321 (orbit link)

Mohit Singh: can you paste a couple of concrete examples (prompt + bad gen)? also was this before/after the kernel-selection/pack change?

Anya Patel: pasted two quick samples below (sanitized). Note system instruction gets cut in the first example.

Anya Patel: ```
SYSTEM: You are a helpful assistant that always follows the user's explicit instructions and never hallucina
User: Summarize the following long document and highlight action items.
===DOCUMENT===
[... ~7k tokens ...]
===END===

Generation: "Sure — here are the action items:
1. Extract key metrics
2. Pare-"
(then model stops, instruction incomplete; appears like the system prefix was truncated mid-word)
```

Anya Patel: second example shows instruction present but later part of the prompt mangled and tokens shuffled: ```
User: Please follow the system instruction above and produce a step-by-step plan.
Generation: "Step 1: Gather data. Step 3: Validate... Step 2: Run tests"
```

Kai Nguyen: hm this smells like a KV buffer wrap / prefix write issue. We changed the circular buffer base index in the kernel selector change in v0.9.3 (commit abc1234). If write_ptr hits kv_size-1 and we handle the wrap incorrectly we could be overwriting early prefix tokens.

Kai Nguyen: can someone grep runtime logs for kv_write_ptr / kv_size around the failing runs? quick check: `grep -E \"kv_(write_ptr|size|read_ptr)\" /var/log/runtime/quant-build/* | tail -n 50`

Mohit Singh: ran a quick grep on the failing run (pulled logs):
```
[2026-10-03T03:12:08Z] runtime: kv_size=8192 kv_write_ptr=8188 write_len=24 -> new_ptr=0 (wrapped)
[2026-10-03T03:12:08Z] runtime: kv_read_ptr=0 kv_dirty=1
[2026-10-03T03:12:08Z] runtime: prefix_len=6202 cache_hits=0
[2026-10-03T03:12:08Z] runtime WARN: prefix_overwritten=true
```
Mohit Singh: looks like a wrap happened at the exact time long prefix was being cached. write_len pushing past boundary -> new_ptr computed to 0 and some early prefix was overwritten.

Jordan Lee: another angle — tokenizer mismatch. Our quantization pipeline used tokenizer v2.1 during model export, but eval harness in nightly uses v2.2 which changed BOS handling for a handful of languages. If token counts differ, prefix packing could push sequences longer than expected and trigger wrap. I repro locally: token counts for the same text differ by ~3 tokens on average for long docs.

Jordan Lee: quick script output: `python -c \"print(len(tok_v2_1.encode(long_text)), len(tok_v2_2.encode(long_text)))\"` -> `6202 6205`

Anya Patel: so probably a confluence: small tokenization delta + change to circular buffer base index -> wrap and overwrite earliest prefix tokens (system instruction). Explains truncated system instruction and shuffled segments.

Mohit Singh: agreed. Proposed triage steps:
- reproduce locally with the exact quantized binary + tokenizer v2.2 and a failing prompt (Anya to attach)
- add instrumentation to runtime to assert prefix integrity after writes (quick sanity check)
- run canary with kernel-selector pinned to previous mapping (rollback kernel change) to verify if spike disappears
- short-term mitigation: disable prefix caching for requests > 6k tokens in canary pool

Anya Patel: attached failing prompt to the eval job and added a rerun link. I'll also add the sample to the repro bucket.

Kai Nguyen: I'll open a runtime issue (runtime#4872) and draft a small patch to bound-check the wrap logic + add an assert. If tests pass, we can fast-follow with a patch release.

Kai Nguyen: snippet of proposed fix: `if (write_len > kv_size - write_ptr) { copy_part1(...); copy_part2(...); /* ensure we don't overwrite read_ptr */ }` — and add explicit check to error if read_ptr would be overwritten.

Mohit Singh: I'll start a canary job to pin kernel-selection to the previous commit and rerun the longctx suite (targeted 200 runs). Scheduling now on dedicated-canary-2.

sre-deploy-bot: Deployment planned: canary/dedicated-canary-2 -> runtime:v0.9.2-kernel-rollback at 2026-10-03T05:00Z (ETA ~15m)

Anya Patel: thanks team. I'll triage tokenizer mismatch in parallel — Jordan, can you dump the tokenizer diffs and open a small ticket to unify the eval harness to the export tokenizer?

Jordan Lee: on it, will open tools#1167 and include tokenization diffs + a small regression test.

Mohit Singh: next steps assigned: runtime patch (Kai), canary run (Mohit), tokenizer harmonize (Jordan), sample + rerun (Anya). If canary removes the spike we'll roll to staging and then prod.

Anya Patel: tagging product & support in case customers saw regressions in nightly: @product @support — preliminary keep-you-posted.

Kai Nguyen: one more note — add an eval that intentionally stresses a near-kv_size prefix length to catch this in future nightly smoke.

Anya Patel: ack. I'll add a focused longctx stress test (single prompt ~7k tokens) into the nightly smoke.

Jordan Lee: low-friction temporary mitigations: bump kv_size by 512 in canary via env override to reduce immediate wrap probability while patch ships. Mohit — can you include that in the canary?

Mohit Singh: done. canary env set kv_size=8704 for the run.

Anya Patel: thanks all. I'll follow up in this thread with repro links + the failing run details once canary completes. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: canary-run-status: queued (dedicated-canary-2). will post results to this thread.

Mohit Singh: quick note — if someone starts a PR, add `cherry-pick-needed` label for the 0.9.x branch. we've seen similar issues in past releases.

Kai Nguyen: will do. opening runtime#4872 now. PR draft incoming.

Anya Patel: ending triage for now — will update when canary finishes or if we get a repro locally. Thanks everyone.
